chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from Tha'labah from Mu'mar ibn Yahya who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about what people narrate from Ali (peace be upon him) regarding certain matters of the private parts, in which he did not command them nor prohibit them, except that he prohibited them for himself and his children. I said, 'How can this be?' He said, 'One verse has made it lawful and another verse has made it unlawful.' I said, 'Does it not happen that one of them has abrogated the other, or are both clear and it is proper to act upon both?' He said, 'He has explained it to you by prohibiting it for himself and his children.' I said, 'What prevented him from explaining that to the people?' He said, 'He feared that they would not obey him. And if Ali (peace be upon him) had established a firm footing, he would have implemented the Book of Allah and all of the truth.'
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali prohibit certain matters for himself but not for the general public?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the concept of *zawāhir* (apparent rulings) versus *khawāṣṣ* (specific practices), where Imam al-Baqir explains that Ali (AS) exercised personal caution (*ihtiyāt*) regarding certain acts due to the coexistence of permissive and prohibitive verses, rather than declaring a definitive *naskh* (abrogation). His self-imposed prohibition served as a practical demonstration of strict adherence to divine law, while his restraint in publicly clarifying the ruling stemmed from a fear that the masses might not fully comply or understand the nuance. This highlights the Imamate's role in preserving the integrity of Sharia through both legal precision and political prudence.

en.sarwar: 8. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hajjal from Tha’labah from Mu’ammar ibn Yahya who has said the following:

“I once asked abu Ja’far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the narration of people from Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in the matters of reproductive issues of human beings about which he did not command or prohibit others except that he prohibited for himself and his children. I asked, ’How can this happen?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is because one verse has made it lawful and the other verse has made it unlawful.’ I then said, ‘This can happen only when one verse cancels the other, or that both are clear and that it is proper to follow both verses. He (the Imam) said, ’He has already explained it by prohibiting it for himself and his children.’ I then asked, ’What prevented him to explain it to people? He (the Imam) replied, ’Because he was afraid of people’s not listening to him. Had Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, been able to establish a strong foothold he would execute all the rules of the book of Allah and all of the truth.’”
